claims.text: The mental model is: skills are reusable instructions, templates, and domain expertise; actions are tool calls that read from or write to systems; MCP is an open protocol for exposing tools and data to AI apps and agents; and agents are the governed workflow wrapper that packages skills, tools, and knowledge together.
Use skills when you need repeatable methodology, domain expertise, or consistent reasoning.
Use custom actions when you need deterministic execution against an internal API, legacy system, or proprietary workflow.
Use MCP when you want open-standard interoperability and reusable tool access across ecosystems.
Use agents when you need scheduled, event-driven, or governed end-to-end workflows.
Skills are reusable packages of instructions, templates, and tools that teach Assistant how to execute specific tasks with domain expertise, and they are loaded only when relevant.
Skills standardize reasoning, actions standardize execution, MCP standardizes interoperability, and agents operationalize all three into production workflows.
FND-104 explains the Glean operating model for search, assistants, and agents, and where each construct fits for customer outcomes.
Glean provides a trusted AI layer over company knowledge, powering enterprise search, assistants, agents, and workflow automation.
Partners differentiate their business with custom agents, connectors, and embedded experiences that create reusable IP and higher-margin offerings.
Technology partners build on Glean's open, extensible platform using APIs, MCP-based tools, embedded experiences, agent extensions, and the connector framework.
The Glean platform spans Search, Assistant, and Agents.
Partner value-creation motions are source, deploy, build, and scale.
